# Tidepool Landing Page: Build Plan

**Global system**
- **Palette:** Sand background (#F5EFE6), ink text (#1B2A33), sea-glass teal primary (#2A7F80), coral for single accents (#E8745A). Alternate sand and teal bands for rhythm.
- **Type:** Fraunces (serif) for headings, Inter for body and UI labels.
- **Motif:** A thin, wavy tide line that divides sections and echoes the product's weekly "rhythm."

**Sections, top to bottom**

1. **Nav.** Sticky, sand background. Wordmark left, three links (Product, Pricing, Log in), teal pill button "Start a week."

2. **Hero.** Two columns. Left: H1 "Plan the week your team actually keeps," one-line subhead naming the Monday-meeting pain, primary "Start free" and secondary "Watch 90-second tour." Right: a tilted product screenshot of the week board inside a rounded frame, with a soft teal tide shape behind it.

3. **Trust strip.** Single row of four to six grayscale team or company names. Caption: "Used by teams of 2 to 15."

4. **Problem.** Full-width ink background, sand text. Three short lines set large in serif, each a recognizable failure: "Tasks live in six threads." "Monday starts with a meeting about the meeting." "Nobody knows what's shipping Friday."

5. **How it works.** Three columns, numbered 01, 02, 03 in coral. Each has a small UI illustration. Copy: "Set the tide" (name the week's goals), "Pool your work" (everyone drops in tasks), "Check the shore" (a five-minute Friday review).

6. **Feature rows.** Two alternating left-right blocks, one screenshot each: shared week board and async check-ins. Body copy under 40 words each, with a plain-language benefit.

7. **Proof.** Warm photo of a small team at a whiteboard, large serif pull quote beside it. Attribute with name, role, and team size.

8. **Pricing.** Three cards on sand. Middle card "Crew" highlighted with teal border. Monthly/annual toggle. Copy stresses "free up to 5 people."

9. **FAQ.** Single-column accordion, five questions: integrations, data export, team size, cancellation, and "Do we need everyone to sign up?"

10. **Final CTA.** Full-bleed teal band. Headline "Your next week starts Monday." Email field and button, with reassurance text beneath: "No card. Set up in four minutes."

11. **Footer.** Ink background, four columns (Product, Company, Resources, Legal), wordmark and a small wave divider at top.

# Tidepool Landing Page: Revised Build Plan

**Strategy**
- **Primary goal:** Free sign-ups from small-team leads (2 to 15 people) who run the weekly planning meeting.
- **Core message:** Tidepool replaces the Monday meeting about the meeting with a shared week everyone can see in five minutes.
- **CTA consistency:** "Start your week free" appears in the nav, hero, pricing, and final band. Secondary actions are always lower-emphasis.

**Global system**
- **Palette:** Sand (#F5EFE6) base, ink (#1B2A33) text, sea-glass teal (#2A7F80) for primary actions, coral (#E8745A) used only for numbers and one highlight per section. Check teal-on-sand and sand-on-ink for WCAG AA.
- **Type:** Fraunces for headings and pull quotes, Inter for body and UI. Body at 18px minimum.
- **Motif:** A single wavy tide line divides sections. It animates subtly on scroll and goes flat under reduced-motion settings.
- **Imagery:** Real product screenshots, never abstract mockups. Team photos are candid, not stock.

**Sections, top to bottom**

1. **Nav.** Sticky sand bar. Wordmark left; Product, Pricing, Log in right; teal pill "Start your week free."

2. **Hero.** Two columns. Left: H1 "Plan the week your team actually keeps." Subhead: "Tidepool gives small teams one shared week, so Monday starts with work, not status updates." Buttons: "Start free" (primary) and "See a real week" (text link opening a short product walkthrough). Right: a tilted screenshot of the week board on a soft teal tide shape.

3. **Trust strip.** Four to six customer logos in grayscale. Caption: "Teams of 2 to 15 use Tidepool to plan every week." Use only logos with permission; omit the strip entirely until you have three.

4. **Problem.** Full-width ink band, sand serif text, three lines in large type: "Tasks live in six threads." "Monday opens with a meeting about the meeting." "Nobody knows what ships Friday." Add one short line beneath in Inter: "Small teams don't need more tools. They need one place to agree."

5. **How it works.** Three columns with coral numerals 01, 02, 03 and a small UI illustration each. "Set the tide" (name the week's two or three goals). "Pool your work" (everyone drops in tasks in under a minute). "Check the shore" (a five-minute Friday review that rolls unfinished work forward).

6. **Feature rows.** Two alternating blocks: shared week board, and async check-ins. Each has a screenshot, a benefit headline, and body copy under 40 words, naming a concrete outcome such as "Stand-ups drop from 30 minutes to 5."

7. **Proof.** Candid photo of a small team at a whiteboard beside a large serif pull quote. Attribute with name, role, team size, and one measurable result.

8. **Pricing.** Three cards on sand. Monthly/annual toggle with "Save 20% annually." Center card "Crew" bordered in teal with a "Most popular" tag. Lead with "Free for up to 5 people, forever."

9. **FAQ.** Single-column accordion, five questions: Integrations, Data export, Team size limits, Cancellation, and "Do we all need accounts?" Answer the last one directly: "No. One lead can set up the week and invite others by link."

10. **Final CTA.** Full-bleed teal band. Headline "Your next week starts Monday." Email field and button "Start your week free," with reassurance beneath: "No card. Set up in four minutes."

11. **Footer.** Ink background, wave divider at top, four columns (Product, Company, Resources, Legal), and a line of copy: "Built for teams who meet on Mondays."

**Mobile:** Sections stack single-column. The hero screenshot moves below the copy, and the CTA stays sticky at the bottom of the screen after the hero.
